snippet.title: Manager level roles: 12 questions you can expect during your interview
snippet.description:
Upcoming Amazon Telephone Screen? Learn how to answer non-technical questions for $50: https://amazoninterview.coach/#services

- First, let me define what I mean by “Manager level” - this usually means the role will be expected to manage employees, and people in general.

Telephone screen - 5 examples:
Have you had any major failures recently?
It is not uncommon to have a 45 minute call diving deeper exclusively on this topic.
How do you start your day? What is it that keeps you excited and going every day?
Motivation.
How do you prioritize workload?
Prioritization is something usually asked in more technical roles. At least this is what I learned.
How do you manage Managers and In-direct reports? How often do you communicate.
Management style. You could ask them this one too, especially in the onsite interview - and if they’re someone possibly part of your future team.
Tell me about one of your projects?
Your most representative project.

Onsite interview:
Tell me about a time when you fired someone
Tell me about a time when you set particularly challenging, yet achievable goals for your team
Tell me about a time when you encouraged a team member to take on a significant risk
Tell me about a time when you set a vision when there wasn’t one? How did you get buy in for this?
Tell me about a time when you felt like your team was not progressing quickly enough. Explain your approach, and the outcome.
Tell me about a time when you had to decide on whether to ask for additional resources for a project. What was the outcome?
Tell me about a time when you helped a team member to achieve a significant goal. What was the outcome?

One final note here, about how to answer these questions. It might sound tempting to always talk about success stories in these context, because, you know, that is quite natural, but, in my opinion, the main goal at this level is to advertise the right type of behavior; which basically means that you should use the most powerful possible story available to answer a question, instead of the more successful one - for example: if you’re asked, tell me about a time when you received negative feedback; the reflex would be to answer with a time when your boss didn’t get what you said, and you explained it and it was fine; an even better one would be when you were actually wrong, but still, you listened to their feedback and followed instructions to regain their trust. This could advertise the right type of behavior much better than if you’d say “they were wrong”.

So the overall idea is not to be afraid of talking about negative stories, if those are better to highlight on the behavior you’re interested to present - of course with the condition not to disqualify you from the job.

snippet.title: 2 Questions for each of Amazon’s 14 Leadership Principles in 2020
snippet.description:
Upcoming Amazon Telephone Screen? Learn how to answer non-technical questions for $50: https://amazoninterview.coach/#services

Looking for someone to role-play before your interview? (free) https://amazoninterview.coach/role-play.php

- The two best interview questions for each of Amazon’s 14 leadership principles.

Customer Obsession
Tell me about a time when you predicted your customer’s needs?
Tell me about a time when you had to deal with a difficult customer?

Ownership
Tell me about a time when you decided to sacrifice short-term gain for long term-success for your company
Provide an example of when you personally demonstrated ownership.

Invent and Simplify
Tell me about a time when you had a challenging situation in which you had to find an alternative approach.
Tell me about a time when you found a simple solution to a difficult problem?

Are Right, A Lot
Tell me about a time when you made a bad decision.
Tell me about a time when you did not have enough data to make the right decision.

Learn and Be Curious
Tell me something interesting you've learned recently.
Describe a time when you were challenged to think differently in order to find a better solution to a problem

Hire and Develop the Best
Tell me about a time when you coached someone.
How do you help your employees to grow?

Insist on the Highest Standards
Tell me about a time when you relentlessly worked on improving the quality of a fully working product, service or process
Tell me about a time when you refused to compromise your standards

Think Big
Tell me about a time when you took on a big risk, because you focused on long term thinking
Tell me about a time when you successfully pitched an idea to global stakeholders

Bias for Action
Tell me about a time you had to quickly adjust your work priorities to meet changing demands.
Tell me about a time when you were working on a tough deadline and you did not have the time to consider all options

Frugality
Tell me about a time when you requested additional resources for a project
How do you make tradeoffs between quality and costs?

Earn Trust
Tell me about a time when you received tough feedback from your manager. How did you respond?
Tell me about a time when you uncovered a significant people problem in your team

Dive Deep
Tell me about a time when you had a complex problem that required a lot of in-depth analysis
Tell me about a time when you had to investigate a challenge in your team

Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit
Tell me about a time when you disagreed with your boss
Tell me about a time when you raised an uncomfortable issue in an internal meeting

Deliver Results
Tell me about a time when you, as a manager, have set a challenging goal in a project or initiative
Tell me about a time when you were 75% through a project and had to pivot strategy
